assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix a positive integer n, an integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and a real x with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n. By L1, floor(n*x) = j. By L2 with t = n*x - j, we get 0 <= t < 1 and x = T_{n,j}(t). By L5, G_{n,j}(t) <= G_{n,j}(0). By L4, G_{n,j}(t) = F_n(x) and G_{n,j}(0) = F_n(j/n). Therefore F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n). Since n, j, and x were arbitrary under the stated hypotheses, this is exactly the theorem.
